name: Real Estate & Construction
summary: Smarter property and construction management software.
description: Real estate and construction UI UX design: property search and listings, project tracking dashboards and field-ready mobile apps for agents and site teams.
image_alt: Glass office towers seen from below, real estate and construction industry
overview:
Property and construction software serves very different people. A buyer comparing listings on a phone, a property manager chasing repairs and a site manager logging progress between tasks all need the product to work for them, often in a hurry and away from a desk. My job is to make each of those moments clear and quick.

I work with founders and product teams on web and mobile products, from the first prototype to a design system that engineers can build from directly. I research with the people who will use the product, so field screens, approvals and dashboards fit how the work is actually done.

challenges.title: Search that converts
challenges.text: Buyers and renters give up when filters, maps and listing details are slow or hard to compare.

challenges.title: Work away from desks
challenges.text: Site teams use phones outdoors, with poor signal and little time, so screens must be simple and quick.

challenges.title: Many roles, one product
challenges.text: Owners, tenants, contractors and managers each need a different view of the same property or project.

challenges.title: Documents and approvals
challenges.text: Drawings, contracts and change orders pile up unless the product makes status and ownership obvious.

faqs.question: What kinds of real estate and construction products do you design?
faqs.answer: Property search and listing platforms, property management portals, construction project dashboards and field apps for site teams, on web and mobile.

faqs.question: Can you design apps for teams working on site?
faqs.answer: Yes. I design field screens with large touch targets, short forms, photo capture and offline states, so people can log work quickly even with poor signal.

faqs.question: How do you handle so many different user roles?
faqs.answer: I map each role and what it needs to see and do early on, then design shared components with role-based views, so the product stays consistent without showing everyone everything.

faqs.question: Can you work with our existing design system?
faqs.answer: Yes. I can extend and clean up an existing system, or create one from scratch with tokens and components that match your codebase.

faqs.question: How do we start?
faqs.answer: Send me a short brief through the contact page. We will have a call about your product, users and timeline, and I will come back with a plan and quote.
